claims: NASA is targeting the launch of the Artemis II mission for April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Pad 39B.
Artemis II will be the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts to test the SLS rocket and Orion capsule.
A 50s YouTube video by Ellie in Space published on Feb 22, 2026 explains why the Artemis II launch was delayed.
The mission goal of Artemis II is to verify deep space capabilities, ensuring the systems can safely support humans before future lunar landings.
The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Additional launch opportunities for Artemis II are available through early April.
A primary backup window for the Artemis II launch is in late April if needed.
